verdict.rationale: Sill detects when the Mac is holding frames back and tells the device, which shows a notice and offers a quality the link can carry (sill-gh-13). Remote sessions start at a quality suited to slower connections (sill-docs-4), and users can pick a Quality level on the device or the Mac (sill-docs-10). Adaptation is a suggestion the user must accept rather than automatic, and the only documented manual control is a single Quality setting, not separate resolution and frame-rate controls. missing for 10: automatic adaptation when the link falls behind, separate user-set resolution and frame-rate controls, independent corroboration.
